title: The demon who kept changing shape

card.keepWhy: He kept changing shape. She kept going.
sources: Devi Mahatmya (part of the Markandeya Purana), chapters 2-3: the gods’ combined radiance becomes the Goddess; she rides a lion and bears the gods’ weapons; Mahishasura changes from buffalo to lion to a man with a sword to an elephant and back to a buffalo before she slays him
Navaratri, nine nights of the Goddess, and Vijayadashami (Dussehra), the tenth day of victory
check: Nine nights of battle and victory on the tenth day are festival tradition rather than the Devi Mahatmya’s own timeline; confirm the film’s wording.
In much of North India, Dussehra celebrates Rama’s victory over Ravana; in Bengal and elsewhere the tenth day honors Durga. Confirm the lesson’s “Dussehra, the day of victory.”

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever quit a bad habit, and it came back in another form? off one app, on to the next.
options: then this goddess is for you. listen.
then this one’s right on time. listen.
good. keep this one for when it does.

steps.line: A demon named Mahishasura could beat any god.

steps.q: No god can beat Mahishasura alone. What do you guess the gods do?
steps.why: In the Devi Mahatmya, fierce light pours out of each god and gathers into one blazing form: the Goddess.

steps.line: So all the gods pooled their power, and from it came Durga, riding a lion, holding a weapon in each of her many arms.

steps.q: In many tellings, Mahishasura had won a boon: no man or god could kill him. Why does that matter here?
o: Only a goddess could defeat him
He could only die by his own hand
He had to be tricked out of it
steps.why: He asked to be safe from every male, sure no woman could threaten him. Many Hindus tell it with a smile: that was his mistake.

steps.line: She faced Mahishasura for nine nights.
steps.label: Navaratri

steps.q: She strikes the buffalo, and he slips out of it into a new shape. What do you guess he becomes first?
steps.why: A lion, then a man with a sword, then an elephant, then a buffalo again (Devi Mahatmya, chapter 3). A lion, against the goddess who rides one.

steps.line: And he kept changing shape: a buffalo, a lion, a man with a sword, an elephant, then a buffalo again.
Every time he changed, Durga kept going. On the tenth day, she won.
steps.label: Dussehra

steps.q: Why does it matter that Durga didn’t stop when he changed shape?
o: Changing shape meant he was weakening
Each shape needed a new kind of weapon
Each new shape was still the same enemy
steps.why: A buffalo, a lion, a man, an elephant: it was always him. She kept her eyes on the demon, not the disguise.

steps.q: The tenth day, Dussehra, also marks another famous victory in much of India. Whose?
steps.why: In much of north India, Dussehra celebrates Rama over Ravana, with huge effigies burned at dusk. In Bengal, the same days are Durga Puja.

steps.line: Old habits change shape. Notice the new disguise, and keep going.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. durga didn’t win on day one. she won because she didn’t stop when the demon changed shape.
hindus honor durga as shakti, divine power, the mother who protects. at navaratri many worship her for nine nights, and celebrate her victory on the tenth day.

steps.q: Mahisha means buffalo. He took many shapes, so why do you think he’s still named Mahishasura, the buffalo demon?
o: He was king of all the buffaloes
He began as a buffalo and kept coming back to it
The buffalo was the first shape Durga defeated
steps.why: First shape, last shape: a buffalo. Old habits often come back to where they started. Durga saw through every disguise.

today.say: name one habit that keeps coming back in new forms. today, catch it once in its new disguise, and keep going. at navaratri many hindus pray to durga for strength. you can learn a short prayer to her, join in, or just remember her lion. it’s your choice.
options: then watch for its next disguise. you’ve got this.
durga faced him nine nights. losing a round isn’t losing.
